open_points.subject: expense correction authorization and validation order
open_points.text: A4 says, “Every project-scoped operation evaluates, in order: valid unexpired unrevoked session … Registry lifecycle policy,” while A7 says, “An expense correction checks its total first, then the expense, then the allocation instructions.”
open_points.question: Does A4’s complete authorization guard run before the correction’s total check, or is the total checked before authorization?
options: Run the complete A4 guard first, then check total, expense and allocations.
Check the total first, then run authorization and the remaining correction checks.
open_points.default_guess: Run the complete A4 guard first, treating A7’s order as the order inside an already-authorized correction.

witness.initial: An active project and expense exist, but the caller has an expired staff session.
events: The caller submits an expense correction with a negative corrected total.
outcomes: A4-first implementation returns the concealed authentication rejection without evaluating the total.
A7-literal implementation returns HTTP 422 for the refused total before rejecting authentication.
witness.observer: The caller observes different HTTP outcomes.

open_points.subject: validation within corrected allocation instructions
open_points.text: A7 says only, “then the allocation instructions”; M26 requires a non-empty list whose signed amounts sum to the corrected total, while M29 also requires every section to belong to the expense’s project.
open_points.question: In what order are allocation-list non-emptiness, instruction shape, signed sum equality, and section-project membership checked during correction?
options: Check non-emptiness and shape, then sum equality, then section membership.
Check non-emptiness and shape, then section membership, then sum equality.
Treat all allocation checks as one unordered validation phase.
open_points.default_guess: Check non-emptiness and shape first, sum equality second, and section membership last.

witness.initial: An authorized operator corrects an existing expense in an active project; section lookup is temporarily unavailable.
events: The operator supplies a non-empty allocation list whose amounts do not sum to the corrected total and whose section identifier requires a repository lookup.
outcomes: A sum-first implementation returns HTTP 422 without attempting the unavailable lookup.
A membership-first implementation attempts the lookup and returns a storage-unavailable failure.
witness.observer: The operator sees 422 in one implementation and a dependency failure in the other.

open_points.subject: required correction payload when total is unchanged
open_points.text: A7 says, “An expense correction checks its total first … then the allocation instructions,” while M28 says only that “an amount correction and the matching allocation adjustment are one atomic operation.”
open_points.question: Must every supplier/date correction carry a corrected total and a complete replacement allocation list, or are total and allocations required only when the amount changes?
options: Every correction must carry total and a complete non-empty replacement allocation list.
A supplier/date-only correction may omit total and allocations and preserves both unchanged.
Total may be supplied without allocations when unchanged, but a changed total requires allocations.
open_points.default_guess: Allow supplier/date-only corrections to omit total and allocations; require both together when changing the amount.

witness.initial: An active-project expense has total EUR 100 and valid stored allocations summing to EUR 100.
events: An authorized operator submits a correction changing only the supplier name and supplies no total or allocation instructions.
outcomes: The correction succeeds and preserves the total and allocations.
The correction is refused with HTTP 422 because total or allocations are mandatory.
witness.observer: The operator sees whether the supplier-only correction succeeds.
